name: Kaus Australis
description: A dwarf of type A0 V 43.9 parsecs away, 6.8 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Narrabri intensity interferometer.

paper.credit: Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417

radius.source: Computed here, not printed by a paper: 6.8 +/- 0.29 solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.44 +/- 0.06 mas of Hanbury Brown, Davis & Allen (1974), MNRAS 167, 121 (the Narrabri intensity interferometer; Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, Table 1, and the JMDC) and the Hipparcos parallax 22.76 +/- 0.24 mas (van Leeuwen 2007, XHIP)

temperature.source: Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, HD 169022: effective temperature 9460 +/- 220 K (Table 6), from the measured angular diameter and the star's flux from the ultraviolet to the infrared

radialVelocity.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331, XHIP, HIP 90185: RV -15 +/- 3.7 km/s (quality B)

distance.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry, HIP 90185: the Hipparcos parallax (van Leeuwen 2007) the radius is computed with, 22.76 +/- 0.24 mas, inverted

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

text.card: A dwarf of type A0 V, 44 parsecs away: 6.8 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 1.44 milliarcseconds, which at its distance is 6.8 solar radii, and its surface is at 9,460 K.
text.locator: Tables 1 and 6, HD 169022: MK type, limb-darkened diameter, effective temperature
